subject: Scheduling: Model serving immersion (60-75m) & agenda
messages:
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@finex.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: procure@finex.com
Date: Tue, 02 Feb 2027 15:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery — Finex inference goals (recap)

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for the discovery call this morning. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned:
- Primary goal: move our core recommendation engine to a hosted inference solution to reduce p99 latency and control costs.
- Typical request: batch + low-latency scoring, mixture of short prompts and ~1k token contexts.
- Constraints: HIPAA-adjacent data flows, strict audit/logging requirements, procurement and security reviews.

We’d like to schedule the next session with your infra/SE team for a deep-dive — roughly 60–75 minutes — to walk through model serving options, KV cache/latency expectations, and deployment patterns. Can you propose 2–3 slots next week?

Also please share an agenda so we can loop in our ML infra and procurement folks.

Cheers,
Lisa
Director of ML Engineering
Finex Systems
[Phone omitted]

Hi Lisa —

Great to hear the recap — that matches our notes from the call. Thanks for outlining the constraints up front; we’ll make sure the session covers compliance-relevant topics and auditability.

Proposed next steps:
1) 60–75 minute Model Serving Immersion with Redwood SE + ML Infra. Intended audience: your ML infra lead, 1-2 data scientists, and procurement/security for the last 15 minutes.
2) Goal: map our serving patterns to your request mix, validate latency/cost tradeoffs, and go over required security artifacts (SOC2, KMS integrations, audit logs).
3) Pre-reads attached: model-serving-immersion-agenda.pdf (outline) and infra-readiness-checklist.xlsx (questions to make the session actionable).

Available slots (PST) next week:
- Tue 9 Feb: 10:00–11:15 or 15:00–16:15
- Wed 10 Feb: 08:30–09:45
- Thu 11 Feb: 13:00–14:15

If none of those work, send a couple of alternatives and we’ll adjust. Please let us know who from Finex will attend so Marcus and Olga can tailor the demo surface (e.g., bring KV cache examples, quantization/latency benchmarks).

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Evelyn — looping in a bit more detail from the SE side.

Short notes on agenda so Finex can decide the emphasis:
- 0–10m: Introductions + goals (Evelyn + Lisa)
- 10–30m: Workload profile & perf targets (Marcus) — we’ll surface p50/p95/p99 expectations with your example traffic
- 30–55m: Architecture walkthrough (Olga) — routing, KV cache, quantization options, and fallback policies; show how we route by policy across hosted/dedicated/private deployments
- 55–65m: Compliance & ops (Evelyn/Olga) — SOC2 artifacts, audit log granularity, KMS/HSM integration overview
- 65–75m: Q&A + procurement asks (procurement join here)

Prep ask for Finex: please paste or attach a short sample request distribution (tokens per request + qps baseline) and any existing infra constraints (VPC, KMS) — that will help us pick the right kernels/quantization examples for the demo.

I’m available for any of the proposed slots; Marcus will bring a small internal demo with KV cache hit metrics if we get a representative prompt set.

— Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
